text:
Maya: FYI rolled kernel-selector v2 to canary at 09:05 UTC. Initial metrics show host CPU p95 up ~6ms and p99 up ~11%. Looks host-side (parse/stream) not GPU.

Jin: grabbed a quick perf sample from the canary node:
```
# perf top -p <pid>
 21% token_parser::parse_stream
 18% http2::hpack_encode
 13% small_frame_writer::emit
 9% kv_cache::rebind_shard
 6% grpc::writev
```

Chris: kv_cache::rebind_shard is suspicious. Could kernel placements be forcing more KV shard remaps?

Alex: possible. v2 favors ultra-low-latency kernels for short seqs and that appears to split traffic across kernels with different shard affinity. More kernel hops -> shard coldness -> more evictions and extra proto parsing.

Lin: i reproduced locally with a short-seq load (~2k rps). With v2 the avg write syscalls/request ~3.9 vs 1.1 baseline. HPACK ops spike visible in tcpdump. KV hit rate drops ~7% during warmup.

Maya: agree we should temp rollback on canary, then run an A/B where B is affinity-aware kernel selection + ingress coalesce.

Chris: rolling back now. will watch host CPU and evict metrics for next 30m.

perf-bot: [alert] Kernel-selector v2 canary -> host CPU p99 +11%, KV evict rate +8%. TraceID: 2311234567. Suggested mitigations: kernel affinity during warmup, increase minibatch window, ingress small-frame coalescing.

Jin: capturing full flamegraph and pprof (high detail). Uploading links to PERF ticket.

Alex: prototyping affinity heuristic: prefer kernel placements with existing KV shard residency for the first N requests of a session (N configurable). Also propose bumping short-seq batch watermark from 8->16 tokens to reduce churn.

Lin: i can add an ingress coalescer flag that merges up to 4 small token frames into one write (max delay 2ms). Should cut writev/syscall rate and HPACK churn, but we must watch single-request latency.

Maya: good call. add p50/p95 checks to the rollout gate and fail if p95 regresses by >5%.

Chris: rollback completed. early look: host p95 back to baseline within 10m. keeping canary stable for 20m then will start A/B.

Alex: will open PR with affinity knob + batch watermark config. bench harness will include syscall counts, kv-hit-rate, and warmup tail numbers.

Jin: uploading flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/flame/2311234567/zz12. attaching to PERF-1302.

Maya: add alert that triggers if kv-evicts increase >5% during rollouts. Also surface writev syscall rate on the per-canary dashboard.

Lin: note: coalescing might add a small latency tail for single-request flows. we'll gate by p95 and only enable if no harmful regression.

Chris: after A/B, if affinity+coalesce reduces host CPU and keeps latency stable we can roll v2 with flags. otherwise we'll iterate.

Maya: scheduling follow-up sync 2026-03-24 16:00 UTC. owners: Alex (affinity + batching), Lin (ingress coalesce), Jin (flame + load tests), Chris (canary ops). perf-bot created ticket PERF-1302.

perf-bot: [note] Follow-up ticket PERF-1302 created: "kernel-selector warmup affinity + ingress small-frame coalesce".

Maya: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
